title: Finite affine family packaged as a faithfully flat finitely presented algebra
statement: Let $R,A$ be commutative rings, $R\to A$ a ring homomorphism, $I$ a finite set, and $(A\to B_i)_{i\in I}$ homomorphisms of commutative rings. Suppose each $A\to B_i$ is flat [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map] and of finite presentation [def-weil-pbc-finitely-presented-algebra], each composite $R\to B_i$ is of finite type [def-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra], and the maps $\operatorname{Spec}B_i\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum] are jointly surjective on points. Put $B=\prod_{i\in I}B_i$ with the coordinatewise maps $R\to A\to B$, and put $Z=\coprod_{i\in I}\operatorname{Spec}B_i$ in schemes [def-pc-scheme; lem-weil-pbc-scheme-coproduct-family]. The canonical isomorphism $Z\cong\operatorname{Spec}B$ identifies each coprojection with the spectrum of the corresponding projection $B\to B_i$. The component maps induce morphisms $q_Z:Z\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ and $p_Z:Z\to\operatorname{Spec}R$ satisfying $p_Z=(\operatorname{Spec}A\to\operatorname{Spec}R)\circ q_Z$, and these correspond under that isomorphism to the stated coordinate maps. The morphism $q_Z$ is flat [def-weil-flat-morphism], surjective and locally of finite presentation [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation], and $p_Z$ is locally of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. The homomorphism $A\to B$ is faithfully flat [def-weil-pbc-faithfully-flat-ring-map] and of finite presentation, and the composite $R\to B$ is of finite type. The empty family is allowed; its joint surjectivity forces $A=0$, and the empty product is the zero ring.

proof.text: Write $\alpha:R\to A$, $\beta_i:A\to B_i$, and $\gamma_i=\beta_i\circ\alpha$. The coproduct universal property gives $q_Z$ and $p_Z$ from the families $\operatorname{Spec}\beta_i$ and $\operatorname{Spec}\gamma_i$. Their composites with every coprojection agree with those of $(\operatorname{Spec}\alpha)\circ q_Z$, so uniqueness gives $p_Z=(\operatorname{Spec}\alpha)\circ q_Z$. Let $e:Z\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{Spec}B$ be the finite affine coproduct isomorphism, with $e\circ\iota_i=\operatorname{Spec}\pi_i$. For the coordinate maps $\beta=(\beta_i)_i$ and $\gamma=(\gamma_i)_i$, functoriality of $\operatorname{Spec}$ gives $(\operatorname{Spec}\beta)\circ e\circ\iota_i=\operatorname{Spec}(\pi_i\circ\beta)=\operatorname{Spec}\beta_i$ and the analogous equality for $\gamma$. Coproduct uniqueness therefore gives $q_Z=(\operatorname{Spec}\beta)\circ e$ and $p_Z=(\operatorname{Spec}\gamma)\circ e$. Coordinatewise equality gives $\gamma=\beta\circ\alpha$.

proof.text: Apply Flat.SpecMap_iff to each flat ring map beta_i. The coprojections form the open cover sigmaOpenCover, so the source-locality instance Flat.instDescScheme gives Flat q_Z. Under the isomorphism e = sigmaSpec B and the identity q_Z = e followed by Spec beta from Step 1, cancel_left_of_respectsIso gives Flat (Spec beta). This argument also applies to an empty coproduct.

source.place: Tag 01U5, lemma-flat-characterize, applied to the affine replacement; finite-product module flatness as in the cited existing leaf

proof.text: For each target point y, joint surjectivity gives a component i and x in Spec B_i over y. The point iota_i(x) maps to y by Sigma.ι_desc, so q_Z is surjective. Cancel precomposition with the isomorphism e to obtain surjectivity of Spec beta. Together with Step 2, flat_and_surjective_SpecMap_iff gives that beta is faithfully flat, exactly the flat-surjective-spectrum criterion.

Each Spec beta_i is locally of finite presentation by LocallyOfFinitePresentation.SpecMap_iff and the hypothesis on beta_i. The coprojections form an open cover, so IsZariskiLocalAtSource.sigmaDesc gives local finite presentation of q_Z. This is the component-neighbourhood argument of the pointwise definition, including its vacuous empty-source case.

Transport local finite presentation of q_Z across the isomorphism e = sigmaSpec B using cancel_left_of_respectsIso and the coordinate comparison in Step 1. The affine finite-presentation criterion LocallyOfFinitePresentation.SpecMap_iff then gives finite presentation of beta.

Apply HasRingHomProperty.Spec_iff for LocallyOfFiniteType to each gamma_i using the finite-type hypothesis. IsZariskiLocalAtSource.sigmaDesc gives local finite type of p_Z from its component neighbourhoods. Cancel precomposition with e in the comparison of Step 1 and apply the affine finite-type criterion HasRingHomProperty.Spec_iff again. This gives finite type of gamma.

If I is empty, any two elements of the product B agree by function extensionality and elimination of an index. Thus B is a subsingleton ring. Step 3 gives beta faithfully flat; RingHom.FaithfullyFlat.injective implies its underlying function is injective. An injective function into a subsingleton has subsingleton domain, so A is subsingleton too. No nonzero-factor or nonempty-index hypothesis is used anywhere.

lean.statement: theorem finiteAffineFamily_fppfAlgebra (R A : CommRingCat.{u}) (α : R →+* A) (I : Type u) [Finite I] (B : I → CommRingCat.{u}) (β : ∀ i : I, A →+* B i) (hflat : ∀ i : I, (β i).Flat) (hfp : ∀ i : I, (β i).FinitePresentation) (hft : ∀ i : I, ((β i).comp α).FiniteType) (hcover : ∀ y : Spec A, ∃ (i : I) (x : Spec (B i)), Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (β i)) x = y) : IsIso (sigmaSpec B) ∧ (∀ i : I, Sigma.ι (fun j : I ↦ Spec (B j)) i ≫ sigmaSpec B = Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (Pi.evalRingHom (fun j : I ↦ B j) i))) ∧ Sigma.desc (fun i : I ↦ Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom ((β i).comp α))) = Sigma.desc (fun i : I ↦ Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (β i))) ≫ Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom α) ∧ Sigma.desc (fun i : I ↦ Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (β i))) = sigmaSpec B ≫ Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (RingHom.pi β)) ∧ Sigma.desc (fun i : I ↦ Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom ((β i).comp α))) = sigmaSpec B ≫ Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (RingHom.pi (fun i : I ↦ (β i).comp α))) ∧ RingHom.pi (fun i : I ↦ (β i).comp α) = (RingHom.pi β).comp α ∧ Flat (Sigma.desc (fun i : I ↦ Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (β i)))) ∧ Surjective (Sigma.desc (fun i : I ↦ Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (β i)))) ∧ LocallyOfFinitePresentation (Sigma.desc (fun i : I ↦ Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (β i)))) ∧ LocallyOfFiniteType (Sigma.desc (fun i : I ↦ Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom ((β i).comp α)))) ∧ (RingHom.pi β).FaithfullyFlat ∧ (RingHom.pi β).FinitePresentation ∧ (RingHom.pi (fun i : I ↦ (β i).comp α)).FiniteType ∧ (IsEmpty I → Subsingleton A ∧ Subsingleton (∀ i : I, B i))
